stem:
A man is standing at a position X in front of a plane mirror, a distance of \(y\) metre from the mirror as shown in figure. When the man moves 5 m away from the mirror, the new distance between the man and his image becomes 20 metre. What is the value of \(y\)?

(The figure shows a vertical plane mirror on the left. The man stands at point X, a distance \(y\) metre in front of the mirror; an arrow marked 5 m points further away from the mirror, showing the direction in which the man then moves.)

In an optics experiment, with the position of the object fixed, a student varies the position of a convex lens. A graph between the object distance \(u\) and the image distance \(v\), from the lens, is plotted using the same scale for the two axes. A straight line passing through the origin and making an angle of \(45^\circ\) with the x-axis meets the experimental curve at P. The coordinates of P will be

(The figure shows a v-versus-u graph: a curve rising from the axes, and a straight line through the origin at \(45^\circ\) (the line \(v = u\)) intersecting the curve at point P.)

A mirror is broken into two parts and these parts are separated by a distance of 1 cm as shown in figure. The focal length of the mirror is 10 cm. The height of the images (in cm with respect to their optic axis), formed by the two parts of mirror when the object is midway between the two principal axes are

(The figure shows a concave mirror split horizontally into an upper half and a lower half; the two halves are pulled apart so their principal axes are separated by 1 cm. A point object O is placed on the line midway between the two axes, at a distance of 15 cm in front of the mirror.)

In the given diagram, three rays of light pass through focal point \(F_1\) to the converging lens, placed along a vertical line. Which of the following is correct regarding this?

(The figure shows three rays of light diverging from a focal point \(F_1\) on the left and travelling to a vertical converging (convex) lens; \(F_2\) marks the focal point on the other side of the lens.)

options.label: A
options.text: The speed of light rays remains same while entering or leaving the converging lens.

options.label: B
options.text: The speed of light rays decreases when they enter the converging lens.

options.label: C
options.text: The speed of light rays increases when they enter the converging lens.

options.label: D
options.text: The speed of light rays decreases when they leave the converging lens.

To produce an image by a convex lens at the position shown (see figure), the object is needed to be placed

(The figure shows a convex lens with optical centre O. On the principal axis, to the left of the lens, F is marked at point Y and 2F at point X; to the right of the lens, F and 2F are marked, and an inverted image (downward arrow) is drawn standing exactly at the 2F mark on the right.)

Which of the following diagrams gives a correct picture of the refraction of parallel rays of light through a convex (converging) lens?

A) Three rays travelling parallel to the principal axis strike the convex lens; after refraction they converge to a single point at the focus F on the far side, with the central ray (through the optical centre) passing straight through undeviated and the upper and lower rays bending toward the axis to meet it at F.
B) Three parallel rays strike the lens, but after refraction the central ray bends instead of going straight and the lower ray passes straight through; the rays do not all meet cleanly at one focus.
C) Two parallel rays strike the lens and after refraction diverge (spread apart) on the far side instead of converging.
D) Three parallel rays strike the lens, but after refraction the central ray is deviated and the rays cross at a point off the marked focus.

It is found that all the light rays sent from X towards Y reach point Z inside the glass sphere, as shown in figure. The speed of rays in glass cannot be

(The figure shows a glass sphere of centre O surrounded by vacuum. X is at the bottom of the sphere and Y on the right; the radius OY is horizontal and OX is vertical, meeting at a right angle at O. A ray travels from X to the surface point Y, where it is totally internally reflected up to point Z at the top of the sphere instead of escaping into the vacuum.)

Which of the following pictures depicts the correct formation of the image of parallel rays of light incident on a concave mirror, where F marks the focal point at the focal distance from the mirror?

A) Parallel rays incident on the concave mirror reflect and converge to a single point located exactly at the focus F (at the focal distance in front of the mirror).
B) Parallel rays reflect from the concave mirror but converge to a point that lies short of F (between the mirror and the focus, at the object screen), not at the marked focus.
C) Parallel rays reflect and meet at a point right at the object screen close to the mirror, well in front of F.
D) Parallel rays reflect from the concave mirror and cross at a point that does not coincide with the marked focus F.
